packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING - packet-21

EXPOSURE NOTE
No edition, catalogue, earlier transcription or proposed identification was seen. One procedural slip: I ran a
single shell directory listing of the packet folder (file names and sizes only) before reading the rules; it
showed nothing about the text. I did not open packet.json. Nothing below is filled in from memory of any text.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)

Observations
- Two overviews (image-001, image-018) show the two sides of one large parchment sheet, photographed with a
  centimetre ruler along the top; the ruler numerals are upside down in both overviews and the writing in the
  overviews is inverted. The detail images (002-017, 019-034) are supplied rotated so the script is upright.
  Sheet roughly 37-38 cm wide by about 26-27 cm high as photographed.
- The sheet is a bifolium laid open: a vertical fold runs down the middle, with small holes along it. Each half
  carries two columns, so four columns per side. Many lines per column (roughly 55-65; not counted exactly
  because of fading).
- Damage: upper edge torn with large losses into the first lines of several columns; one outer side edge ragged
  with losses into the outer column; a round cut-out and a diagonal cut at one lower corner; small holes
  scattered; heavy staining and abrasion; horizontal and vertical creases; stitching holes / a dashed line along
  one outer edge. This looks like reuse as binding material (tentative interpretation).
- Script: small, highly abbreviated cursive bookhand in pale brown ink. Ruled lines are visible on the faded
  side.
- No running titles seen. No rubrics or coloured ink seen. No enlarged or decorated initials seen. No
  underlining seen. Text is divided by small spaces followed by a recurring "Jt(em)" (very frequent) and, less
  often, "Alii"/"Alij", "dicend(um)", "s(ed) (con)t(ra)(?)". A few short lines end a paragraph and the next line
  begins indented (image-024 lines 1, 6-7; image-032 near the foot).
- Marginal notes: short, faint notes of two or three letters in the central gutter margin between the two
  leaves (image-020 right edge, image-024 right margin at three heights, image-028 right margin). They look like
  brief index words or abbreviations; I could not read them securely (one looks like "q. d."(?), another
  "dic"(?) or "dis"(?)).
- A blind-embossed rectangular stamp with capital letters is in a lower corner (image-034, also the edge of
  image-033). I did not attempt to interpret it.
- Side A (image-001 to 017) is very badly rubbed: most of it is illegible in these images. Side B (image-018 to
  034) is considerably better, especially the outer left column (image-019, 023, 027) and the column next to it
  (image-020, 024).

Tentative interpretations
- The repeated "Jt(em)" + short proposition pattern, with "dicend(um) q(uod)" and "Alii ... dic(un)t", looks
  like a series of brief arguments/notes or a compressed disputation record rather than continuous commentary on
  a lemma. I saw no visibly distinguished lemmata (no underlining, no larger script), so I cannot separate
  "quoted text" from "commentary".
- Column order across the fold and which side is first cannot be determined from the images alone.

2. AREAS SELECTED / NOT READ
Selected (side B): outer left column, upper and middle part (image-019, image-023, image-027); second column,
upper-middle (image-020, image-024); far right column top (image-022).
Selected (side A): right-hand column, upper part (image-009) only, as the least rubbed patch.
Looked at but not transcribed (too faint for a responsible reading): image-002 to 008, 010 to 017 (side A almost
entirely); image-021, 025, 026, 028 to 034 (third and fourth columns of side B and the lower parts), where only
isolated words came out, listed in section 4.
A raking-light or UV/multispectral capture of side A, and tighter crops (2x) of the side B right-hand leaf, would
be needed to go further.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: (..) = my proposed expansion of an abbreviation; ? after a word or inside brackets = uncertain
reading; [illegible] = unreadable; [hole]/[torn] = physical loss. Line numbers count from the top of each image,
including a partly cropped first line. Almost every line is uncertain to some degree; words without "?" are
only relatively more secure. "Jt(em)" is written with a tall J-like I throughout.
